cards.d: An addict is a person who cannot stop doing or having something.
cards.e: She was a coffee addict. She had more than three cups each day.
cards.ielts: Many parents worry that their teenagers are becoming smartphone addicts who cannot put their devices down even during family meals.

cards.d: When something is archeological, it relates to archeology.
cards.e: They found archeological evidence that proved an ancient species of man.
cards.ielts: The construction of the new metro line was delayed for two years after workers uncovered an important archeological site beneath the city centre.

cards.d: Archeology is the study of ancient people through their artifacts.
cards.e: He studied archeology to learn more about ancient Egyptian culture.
cards.ielts: Some students argue that archeology is irrelevant today, but studying ancient societies helps us understand how modern cities and cultures developed.

cards.d: To brainstorm is to have a lot of ideas about a certain topic.
cards.e: The students met after school to brainstorm ideas for their assignment.
cards.uz: aqliy hujum oʻtkazmoq, gʻoyalar oʻylab topmoq
cards.ielts: Before writing an IELTS essay, it is wise to spend five minutes brainstorming arguments for both sides of the question.

cards.d: A budget is the amount of money available to spend on something.
cards.e: His budget for food was very tight.
cards.ielts: Governments with a limited budget must decide whether to spend more on public healthcare or on improving transport infrastructure.

cards.d: When something is chaotic, it is crazy, confused, and hectic.
cards.e: The first day of school can be chaotic for a new student.
cards.ielts: Traffic in many rapidly growing cities has become chaotic, with commuters spending hours stuck in jams every morning and evening.

cards.d: To cite something is to mention it as an example or as proof of something.
cards.e: She cited six reasons that the school needed to build new classrooms.
cards.uz: keltirmoq, iqtibos keltirmoq, misol qilib koʻrsatmoq
cards.ielts: To support their argument, candidates should cite specific examples, such as the success of recycling schemes in Scandinavian countries.

cards.d: To correspond is to match or to be similar to something.
cards.e: The boy’s story didn’t correspond with his mother’s version.
cards.ielts: The rise in obesity rates closely corresponds with the growing consumption of fast food between 1990 and 2020.

cards.d: A courtyard is an outdoor area that is surrounded by the walls of a building.
cards.e: During the summer, the courtyard is a nice place to have lunch.
cards.ielts: My favourite place at university was the quiet courtyard where students gathered between lectures to chat and revise.

cards.d: An estate is a large area of land owned by a family or organization.
cards.e: He lived on his father’s estate in the country.
cards.ielts: The wealthy family donated part of their country estate to the local council so that it could be turned into a public park.

cards.d: Fraud is the crime of gaining money by lying or by tricking people.
cards.e: Experts say that credit card fraud increases around the holidays.
cards.ielts: As more people shop online, banks are investing heavily in technology to detect fraud and protect customers’ personal data.

cards.d: Hydrogen is a gas that has no taste, color, or smell.
cards.e: Balloons filled with hydrogen can easily float away if you aren’t careful.
cards.ielts: Some experts believe that cars powered by hydrogen could significantly reduce air pollution in major cities over the coming decades.

cards.d: Integrity is honesty and good morals.
cards.e: The principal had a lot of integrity.
cards.ielts: Politicians who lack integrity quickly lose public trust, which is why transparency in government spending is so important.

cards.d: To knit is to make fabric by connecting strings together.
cards.e: My grandmother knitted me a sweater.
cards.ielts: In my free time I enjoy knitting scarves, because it helps me relax after a stressful day at work.

cards.d: An outlook is a person’s opinion or way of thinking about something.
cards.e: He changed his outlook about rats after he read a book about them.
cards.ielts: Travelling abroad as a student completely changed my outlook on life and made me more tolerant of other cultures.

cards.d: A parachute is a device that helps people and things fall to the ground safely.
cards.e: They used parachutes dropped from airplanes to send supplies to the civilians.
cards.ielts: During the earthquake relief operation, food and medical supplies were dropped by parachute into villages that roads could not reach.

cards.d: When something is prehistoric, it is from a time when there was no written history.
cards.e: The scientists found prehistoric pots used by the people in the area.
cards.ielts: Museums play a vital role in education by allowing children to see prehistoric tools and learn how early humans survived.

cards.d: A proponent is a person who supports an idea or a plan.
cards.e: He was a proponent of using environmentally friendly products.
cards.ielts: Proponents of remote working claim that it boosts productivity, while critics argue that it weakens teamwork and company culture.

cards.d: To refine something is to make it better by making changes.
cards.e: The principal refined his method of controlling students over the years.
cards.ielts: Over several months, the engineers refined their design until the solar panels were both cheaper and more efficient.

cards.d: To restrict is to limit something and prevent it from getting bigger.
cards.e: The club restricted the amount of members.
cards.ielts: Many governments now restrict the use of plastic bags in an attempt to reduce the amount of waste entering the oceans.
